new_statements.rule_in_words: Karko is analysed as a tone language (high, mid, low; falling and rising contours arising from lost syllables), with tone a property of the syllable and able to mark number on its own; the modern description says nothing about word stress. The only Karko-specific stress remark is Meinhof 1918/19 (ZfK 9: 49-50), who found the stress accent impossible to pin down ('scheinbar willkuerliche Behandlung') and had the impression of musical tones that shift with position in the sentence.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said in any source examined.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Karko proper. For the Tabaq variety (Hellwig & Schneider-Blum 2014: 68, 72, 74, 76) suffix and word-final syllables are called 'unstressed' (site of vowel centralization and shortening) without a stated placement rule; Tabaq has two level tones H/L plus HL/LH contours (p. 77). Meinhof 1918/19: 49-50 (Garko): 'Die Beobachtung des Staerkeakzents ist ausserordentlich erschwert durch die scheinbar willkuerliche Behandlung desselben.. Ich habe den Eindruck, als wenn zwar musikalische Toene vorliegen, als ob sie aber durch die Stellung im Satz sich aendern' [Observation of the stress accent is made extraordinarily difficult by its apparently arbitrary treatment.. I have the impression that musical tones are indeed present, but that they change with position in the sentence].
new_statements.domain_note: Jakobi & Hamdan's tone marking is on citation forms of nouns (sg/pl pairs); no word- vs phrase-level prominence discussion. Meinhof's remark concerns elicited words and short sentences.
new_statements.identity_note: Jakobi & Hamdan 2015 describe Karko proper (kàâŋg / káákmbɛ̀ɛ̀), co-authored by a native speaker. Meinhof 1918/19 'Garko' = Karko (informants from Jebel Garko near Dulman, recorded in El-Obeid 1914). Hellwig & Schneider-Blum 2014 and Ismail 2015 describe Tabaq (t̪àànɪ̀), and Alshareef 2015 describes Abu Jinuk; Glottolog 5.1 files all of these under kark1256 (no separate glottocodes; DoReCo labels the Tabaq corpus 'Tabaq (Karko)'), whereas Ethnologue/Wikipedia note Tabaq and Abu Jinuk 'may be dialects or separate languages'. The Tabaq tone facts (2 tones) should not be transferred to Karko proper (written with H/M/L).

sources.note: Sec. 2 'Phonology, syllable structure, and morphophonemic alternations' (pp. 273-276): vowels, length, vowel harmony, syllable types; data written with H/M/L and falling/rising tones; p.274 'tone is not conceived to be a property of a vowel but rather a property of a syllable'; p.288 sg/pl 'can even be solely marked by tonal contrast'. No statement on word stress anywhere. fn.1: a grammatical sketch of Karko is in Jakobi's ms 'Kordofan Nubian: A Synchronic and Diachronic Study' (to appear).

sources.note: Phonology overview of Tabaq (variety Glottolog files under kark1256). Sec. 4 'Tone' p.77: 'Tabaq has two level tones (high h, low l) that can be combined in one syllable to give a falling (hl) or rising (lh) contour', with minimal pairs and pitch tracks. 'Unstressed syllables' are mentioned in passing as the locus of vowel centralization/shortening (fn.6 p.68; p.72 'suffix vowels are usually short and occur in unstressed syllables'; p.74; p.76 'vowels in word final and unstressed syllables are realized extra short'), implying root/initial prominence, but no explicit rule for where stress fall…
